text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday, prepared for Reuters by the Estonian news agency, ETA. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- Southern Tartu city council voted Mayor Tonis Lukas out of office. A new mayor will be elected in two weeks.

- Public opinion research firm Saar Poll published the results of a poll among non-citizens. It revealed that 25 percent of Russian citizens in Estonia and 59 percent of stateless persons consider Estonia as their home. Nearly 80 percent of the stateless persons desire Estonian citizenship for their children and 94 percent consider inter-ethnic relations good or satisfactory in Estonia.
SONUMILEHT

- Agriculture Minister Andres Vaarik declared that protective tariffs would slow down food price rises instead of accelerating them. The right-wing opposition criticises the planned imposition of protective tariffs on imported pork.
- Former education minister Jaak Aaviksoo announced that Estonia invests 6.6 percent of GNP into education and 88 percent of the education system is state-financed.
EESTI PAEVALEHT
- The police and the roads department are concerned with the large number of overloaded lorries on Estonian roads. A study shows that more than 90 percent of large lorries are overweight.
- Journalist Enno Tammer was found guilty of having used insulting expressions in an interview and was fined 220 kroons plus 1,770 kroons legal expenses.
- Police have arrested a man who shot dead and dismembered his girlfriend after a quarrel about money.
POSTIMEES

- Swedish newspaper Dagens Nyheter published an article accusing the crew of the ferry Estonia which sank in 1994 of incompetence and negligence. The Finnish Helsingin Sanomat, on the contrary, defended the seamen.
- Baltic defence ministers signed a cooperation agreement in Vilnius.
- Prime Minister Mart Siimann wants to appoint Tartu county head Jaan Ounapuu as minister for regional affairs.
ARIPAEV
- Firms applying for registration have had to change their share capital, because the commercial code requires that share capital correspond to net assets.
- Insurance firm Leks has decided to begin selling their shares at the Tallinn exchange.
- The transport ministry asks 155 million kroons for the planned new Tallinn-Tartu road in the next year's budget.
